outline: Microscopic colitis — collagenous and lymphocytic colitis
primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
diagnosis: Collagenous colitis, a subtype of microscopic colitis
mechanism: Microscopic colitis produces chronic watery nonbloody diarrhea despite a grossly normal or near-normal colonoscopy. Collagenous colitis is defined histologically by a thickened subepithelial collagen band with inflammatory cells in the lamina propria; lymphocytic colitis instead has prominent intraepithelial lymphocytosis.
vignette: A 68-year-old woman has 3 months of watery, nonbloody diarrhea, including episodes that wake her from sleep. Stool cultures and testing for enteric pathogens are negative. Colonoscopy shows normal-appearing mucosa throughout the colon. Random biopsies show chronic inflammation with a markedly thickened subepithelial collagen band.
lead: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
distractor_notes: IBS-D can cause chronic diarrhea but does not cause the characteristic histologic thickening of the subepithelial collagen layer and usually does not produce persistent nocturnal inflammatory diarrhea.

Ulcerative colitis typically causes bloody diarrhea and visible continuous mucosal inflammation beginning in the rectum; a grossly normal colon with diagnostic microscopic collagen deposition points elsewhere.
Celiac disease causes small-intestinal villous atrophy, crypt hyperplasia, and intraepithelial lymphocytosis rather than a thickened subepithelial collagen band in colonic biopsies.
Giardiasis can cause prolonged watery or greasy diarrhea but is diagnosed by stool/duodenal testing and does not produce the defining colonic biopsy pattern.
key_expl: Microscopic colitis should be suspected in an older adult with chronic watery nonbloody diarrhea despite a normal colonoscopic appearance. The thickened subepithelial collagen band identifies the collagenous-colitis subtype. Diagnosis requires colonic biopsies because gross mucosal appearance is often normal.
objective: Recognize collagenous microscopic colitis from chronic watery nonbloody diarrhea, normal colonoscopy, and a thickened subepithelial collagen band on biopsy.
